title: Accessible Product Landing Page
description: Build a fully accessible landing page for a product, applying semantic HTML, alt text, form labels, keyboard navigation, and contrast.
problemStatement:
## Project: Accessible Product Landing Page

You are designing the landing page for **EcoBottle**, a reusable water bottle. The page must attract customers and allow them to sign up for a newsletter. 

### Core Requirements
- Use semantic HTML5 throughout (`<header>`, `<nav>`, `<main>`, `<section>`, `<footer>`).
- A **skip navigation** link that jumps to the main content.
- A clear **heading hierarchy** (only one `<h1>`).
- At least three **images** (product photo, icon, decorative background) with appropriate `alt` text (informative, empty, etc.).
- A **navigation bar** with three links, properly marked up with `<nav>` and `<ul>`.
- A **sign‑up form** containing:
  - Email input with a visible `<label>` and proper association.
  - A required checkbox for terms with associated `<label>`.
  - A submit button (native `<button>`).
- All form fields must have accessible error messages shown on attempted submission with empty/invalid values (use `aria-describedby` and `aria-invalid`).
- **Color contrast** must pass WCAG AA (at least 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text and UI components). Provide a CSS that meets this.
- Full **keyboard operability**: all interactive elements must be reachable and usable via Tab/Enter/Space, with visible focus indicators.
- The page must be **responsive** and not require horizontal scrolling at 320px width.
- No ARIA attributes that duplicate native semantics (e.g., no `role="button"` on a `<button>`).

### Deliverable
A single HTML file with embedded CSS (and minimal JS for form validation) that passes **axe DevTools** with zero violations and a manual keyboard test.
requirements: Skip to main content link (visible on focus)
All images have appropriate `alt` attribute (informative, decorative, or functional)
Newsletter sign‑up form with accessible labels, error handling, and `aria-invalid`/`aria-describedby`
WCAG AA contrast for text and UI components
Keyboard accessible: Tab order logical, visible focus indicator, no traps
hints: Use the `:focus-visible` pseudo‑class to style focus indicators, not just `:focus`, and avoid `outline: none` without a replacement.
For form validation, prevent default submission, check fields, inject error messages into linked `<span>` elements, and move focus to the first invalid field.
Test with the WAVE tool or axe DevTools to catch any structural issues early.
Remember: a decorative background image should have `alt=""`.
To meet contrast, avoid light grey on white; use a color contrast checker.
expectedOutput: A single HTML file (or HTML/CSS/JS) that renders a visually clean, accessible landing page. Example URL: localhost.
